column1: # Canonical OpenRouter model allowlist for the manual QA stack.
# Format: <openrouter-slug><TAB><display name>  (comment lines start with #)
# Semantics:
# - bifrost-provision.sh seeds the gateway's `openrouter` provider key with
#   exactly these slugs (so the key only ever authorizes QA models).
# - wire-opencode-config.sh writes the opencode provider models map from
#   this file: the opencode id is `openrouter/<slug>`, used as
#   `bifrost/openrouter/<slug>` in config `model` values.
# - ORDER MATTERS: this is the enumeration order the CLI wizard sees, so
#   the keyword-priority ordering assertions of TC-CLI-02 read the same
#   order as `SUBAGENT_RECOMMENDATIONS` (deepseek/qwen = strong tier,
#   mimo/gemini = cheap tier). Keep the rows tier-mixed exactly like this.
# - Keep the list <= 7 models: the wizard's per-agent prompt folds after
#   seven entries.
# - Before changing an id, confirm it still exists and still supports
#   tool calling: curl -s https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models
#   (the suite's flows require tool calls; TC-LLM-02 proves it).
# Costs (per 1M tokens, prompt/completion, as of 2026-08-26): the deepseek
# and qwen rows are a few cents; claude-sonnet-5 is the most expensive
# entry and gpt-5.6-luna is mid-tier. The per-group model under test is
# selected with BIFROST_MODEL, see qa/README.md.
deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
qwen/qwen3.5-plus-20260420
xiaomi/mimo-v2.5
google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite
anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
openai/gpt-5.6-luna
